 5 K-dramas for when you’ve had a long day but still want “just one more episode”
 Five K-dramas that make “just one more episode” very easy after a long day.
 By Jeff Souza • @papodedorama @papodedorama • Published on 27.10.2026 at 06:01 
 Image for 5 K-dramas for when you’ve had a long day but still want “just one more episode”. 
 Read in: 
 Portuguese 
 English 
 Español Some days, even choosing what to watch feels like work. That is when it helps to have a story that does not need three episodes to prove why it is worth continuing. These five K-dramas do that in different ways: through comedy, small everyday problems or one question that becomes hard to leave unanswered.
 PapoResumo The essentials in a few seconds The selection matches viewing moods, from A Business Proposal for easy laughs to Between Steps for a slower pace.
 Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha grounds its humor in practical mishaps: Hong Du-sik offers squid-cleaning work instead of lending Yoon Hye-jin 4,000 won.
 King the Land builds workplace friction around Cheon Sa-rang maintaining her required smile while Gu Won rejects that same professional expectation.
 Automatic summary based only on this article. Warning: this list discusses events from Episode 1, including secret identities, investigations and early story conflicts. 1. Between Steps starts small — and that is exactly why it works
 Kim So-hyun and Choo Young-woo as Im Yoo-jin and Park Min-jae in Between Steps. (Disney+) Park Min-jae’s days revolve around medical checkups and the robotics lab until his friends start making lists of things they still want to do. He adds “start dating” to his. Earlier, he had already helped Im Yoo-jin at a bus stop after a problem with her shoe and reminded her that there would always be another bus. Between Steps turns small decisions into reasons to see what comes next.
 Publicidade Where to watch: Disney+ .

 2. A Business Proposal lets the lie get out of control fast
 Ahn Hyo-seop and Kim Se-jeong in A Business Proposal. Image: SBS. Shin Ha-ri goes on a blind date in place of her friend and plans to be unpleasant enough to end the whole thing that night. Then she discovers that Kang Tae-moo is the president of the company where she works. The question immediately changes: how long can Ha-ri keep her real identity hidden? Once Tae-moo starts talking about marriage, the mess has already grown far beyond the original favor. A Business Proposal tells its story in 12 episodes.
 Where to watch: Netflix .
 3. Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha turns a bad day into a reason to stay
 Shin Min-a and Kim Seon-ho in a scene from Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha. Promotional image. Yoon Hye-jin arrives in Gongjin and suddenly finds herself unable to use her card, phone or an ATM. When she needs 4,000 won to pay for a coffee, she asks Hong Du-sik for help. He does not lend her the money — he finds her a job cleaning squid instead.
 The humor comes from these small disasters and Du-sik’s practical response to each one. By the time Hye-jin decides to open a dental clinic in the village, the story has already found its next reason to keep going.
 Where to watch: Netflix .
 4. King the Land puts two opposite ideas in the same hotel
 Lim Yoon-a and Lee Jun-ho star in King the Land. Image: JTBC. Cheon Sa-rang joins the King Hotel determined to do her job well and keep the smile the job demands. Gu Won returns to the same hotel hating exactly that kind of obligatory smile.
 Publicidade The episode also follows Sa-rang through some far less glamorous tasks before she earns her place at the hotel. By the time the two realize they will have to deal with each other, the next conflict is already waiting.
 Where to watch: Netflix .
 5. Love in Disguise trades comfort for curiosity
 Im Si-wan and Seol In-ah star in Love in Disguise, which mixes romance, investigation and a secret identity. Credit: tvN. This is the most tense entry on the list. Kang Jae-hee is investigating Yoon Yi-jun, a suspect in the death of his former secretary, when she applies to work for him while disguised as a man.
 The interview goes badly, but a chaotic encounter soon afterward changes Yi-jun’s decision. She needs to watch him without exposing who she really is; he expects complete loyalty from his new employee. That setup leaves a clear question hanging over the next episode.
 For more on the setup, cast and investigation, Papo de Dorama has a full guide to Love in Disguise .
 Where to watch: Prime Video .
 If you want something easy to laugh along with, A Business Proposal is the most direct choice. If you would rather slow down without losing momentum, Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha and Between Steps fit better. And if a long day leaves you wanting curiosity instead of comfort, Love in Disguise gets there quickly.
